text:
sam: noticed a weird memory climb on staging when long-context chat runs hit continuous batching. p99 jumps ~30% and RSS creeps over several minutes :thinking_face:
alisa: can you paste the profile flamegraph? is it the KV cache or decoder?
mohit: looking at heap samples — KV slab allocations keep growing, not freed. Looks like fragments are being pinned by batches that keep merging/splitting.
sam: here's a short repro log from a trace run (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-16T14:02:03Z] contbatch: merge start id=3726 size=9 -> merged 2 small batches
[2026-03-16T14:02:03Z] kv: alloc slot=0x7f9e4a stride=4096 pages=3
[2026-03-16T14:02:03Z] kv: pin slot=0x7f9e4a refcnt=1 owner=batch-3726
[2026-03-16T14:02:04Z] contbatch: split triggered id=3726 -> sizes (7,4)
[2026-03-16T14:02:04Z] kv: slot remained pinned, not evictable
[2026-03-16T14:02:06Z] mem: RSS +18MB
[2026-03-16T14:02:12Z] metrics: p99_latency +28%\n```
jun: hmm, the stride allocation is weird — a lot of small fragments (3 pages) rather than compact allocations. When contbatch splits, references don't move to the new owner, so the old fragment stays pinned until GC.
alisa: profile snapshot: top flame shows kv::alloc -> kv::pin -> batch::hold for ~9s. CPUP samples show minimal CPU, it's a memory residency issue.
mohit: reproducer attached: longctx length ~16k tokens, batch rate 150/s, contbatch aggressive merge threshold 10. If we reduce merge threshold to 4, memory stabilizes.
sam: concrete hypothesis: merge merges requests across different contexts creating interleaved KV segments; split leaves 'stale' fragment handles that keep pages live because refcounting is per-slot but ownership transfer isn't happening on split. result = fragmentation + slow compaction.
jun: agree. Also saw head-of-line blocking: long tail batches that hold slots block eviction threads waiting for slot->unlock. Eviction tries to reclaim but sees refcnt>0 and spins on wait queue. :eyes:
alisa: quick mitigation options: 1) eagerly transfer ownership on split, decrement old slot refcnt; 2) mark split fragments as 'detachable' and allow background compactor to coalesce; 3) add short lease expiry for pinned slots when owner is a split transient.
mohit: implementation note: (2) is lowest risk. background compactor can run at low priority and try to merge neighbor fragments if both are detachable. need O(1) neighbor lookup.
sam: can we add a contbatch metric: split_count, stale_slot_count, avg_stale_lifetime? would help quantify.
jun: yes, I'll add counters and histograms. also add a gauge for 'kv_fragmentation_ratio = total_fragment_pages / used_pages'.
alisa: quick patch idea: in batch split path, do:
```
if (old_slot.owner != new_owner) {
  old_slot.refcnt--;
  new_slot.refcnt++;
  if (old_slot.refcnt == 0 && old_slot.detachable) schedule_compact(old_slot);
}
```
works in theory but must be careful with races with eviction thread.
mohit: test plan: unit test for split ownership transfer, integration perf test with longctx synthetic workload, and run on staging for 12h. Also validate p99 token latency and RSS.
sam: can we also tune kernel selection? maybe some models' kv layout leads to smaller strides -> more frag. But fix should be in contbatch/kv layer first.
jun: I'll prototype a background compactor + metric PR. aiming for PR by EOD tomorrow. runtime-bot: perf-test/contbatch-longctx started (id: pt-8892). ETA 3h.
alisa: great. if pt-8892 shows lower stale_slot_count after compactor, we can backport to canary. :thumbsup:
mohit: one more note — watch for NUMA effects; compaction that touches pages may cause CPU spike and page migration; compactor needs to rate-limit page touches to avoid perf blips.
sam: agreed. add a pacing limiter. thanks everyone — follow-up sync tomorrow after perf run.
